purpose: Turn a broad Legal, Health, Home or Auto need into a private, review-ready preparation packet with responsible local starting routes.

legal.label: Legal preparation
legal.boundary: General organization only—not legal advice, representation, a deadline calculation, a filing or a prediction. Verify Tennessee rules and dates with the responsible source or a qualified professional.
legal.todayBoundary: If safety is at risk, call 911. If papers, a hearing or a stated deadline may require action today, contact the responsible Tennessee court, agency or a qualified attorney now.

tracks.title: Notice and deadline organizer
tracks.summary: Separate what a document says from what still needs verification.
steps: Identify the document type and issuing organization without uploading it.
Write down every printed date exactly as shown.
Confirm the responsible Tennessee court or agency from an official source.
List the action the document appears to request without interpreting it.
Prepare questions for a qualified review before relying on a deadline.
questions: Which date controls and how can I verify it?
What response options exist?
What should I bring to a qualified review?

tracks.title: Facts and records preparation
tracks.summary: Create a neutral sequence of dates, records and open questions.
steps: List dates and events in time order using neutral language.
Separate records you have from records you may need.
Mark each statement as observed, documented or uncertain.
Remove passwords, account numbers and unnecessary private details.
Prepare a short review agenda instead of a legal conclusion.
questions: Which facts are most important to verify?
Which records are usually useful?
What should I avoid sharing on an unsecured channel?

tracks.title: Attorney or advocate review preparation
tracks.summary: Prepare for a focused first conversation without choosing or ranking a professional for you.
steps: Choose the broad issue area and Tennessee location.
List immediate safety, hearing or response concerns first.
Prepare a neutral one-page chronology.
Write questions about scope, fees, conflicts, timing and next steps.
Verify credentials, fit and availability directly.
questions: Is this within your practice and jurisdiction?
What does your engagement include and cost?
What should happen before the next important date?

tracks.title: Local legal-help search plan
tracks.summary: Search by issue and geography while keeping directory order neutral.
steps: Choose the broad legal issue.
Confirm whether Franklin, Williamson County, Tennessee or federal geography matters.
Search source-backed profiles without treating order as a ranking.
Compare the same public facts for up to three listings.
Verify practice, credentials, fees and availability directly.
questions: Do you handle this type of Tennessee matter?
Do you serve Franklin or Williamson County?
What information is safe to share before engagement?

health.label: Health access and affordability
health.boundary: General access preparation only—not diagnosis, treatment, eligibility, coverage or benefit advice. Call 911 for an emergency and call or text 988 for a mental-health or substance-use crisis.
health.todayBoundary: For emergency symptoms or immediate danger, call 911. For a mental-health or substance-use crisis, call or text 988. For urgent non-emergency care, contact a responsible provider or insurer directly.

tracks.title: Coverage change readiness
tracks.summary: Organize plan, provider and medication questions before a coverage transition.
steps: Identify the broad type of coverage change.
List current providers and prescriptions without entering identifiers here.
Confirm effective dates and notices directly with the plan.
Ask about continuity, appeals and accessible communication.
Record confirmation numbers privately after contacting the responsible organization.
questions: When does the change take effect?
How do I verify provider and prescription coverage?
What review or complaint rights apply?

tracks.title: Medication cost and access preparation
tracks.summary: Prepare safe questions about coverage, alternatives and assistance without changing medication advice.
steps: Use an exact medication list privately, not on this page.
Confirm formulary, pharmacy and prior-authorization facts with the plan.
Ask the prescriber or pharmacist about clinically appropriate options.
Check qualified assistance routes and current eligibility directly.
Do not stop or change medication based on this planner.
questions: Is this medication covered at my pharmacy?
What approval steps apply?
Which assistance sources can I verify?

tracks.title: Preventive and lower-cost care plan
tracks.summary: Compare appropriate care starting points and cost questions without diagnosing urgency.
steps: Choose preventive, routine, same-day or follow-up care.
Use emergency routes first when symptoms may be urgent.
Ask about total expected cost, insurance and sliding-scale policies.
Confirm credentials, accessibility and appointment availability.
Prepare records and questions without uploading health information.
questions: Is this the right care setting?
What will I likely owe?
What should I bring?

tracks.title: Dental, vision or adult-care transition
tracks.summary: Prepare continuity, records and access questions across a care transition.
steps: Choose dental, vision or transition-to-adult care.
List current providers and records privately.
Confirm network, referral and age-transition requirements.
Ask how records transfer and who coordinates follow-up.
Verify accessibility, cost and appointment details directly.
questions: What changes at this transition?
How are records transferred?
Who coordinates the next appointment?

home.label: Home and property preparation
home.boundary: General project and issue preparation only—not legal advice, code interpretation, permit approval, contractor endorsement or a property-value prediction. Verify jurisdiction and requirements directly.
home.todayBoundary: For fire, gas, structural danger, flooding near electricity or immediate danger, call 911 or the responsible emergency utility. For a posted notice or lockout concern, seek qualified help promptly.

tracks.title: Permit and zoning readiness
tracks.summary: Organize project scope and jurisdiction questions before filing or construction.
steps: Describe the project in broad, factual terms.
Confirm the exact property jurisdiction.
Ask which permits, reviews and inspections may apply.
Separate city, county, utility and association requirements.
Do not begin regulated work based only on this packet.
questions: Which authority controls this address?
Which approvals may be required?
What must happen before work begins?

tracks.title: Buying or selling preparation
tracks.summary: Prepare questions about title, disclosures, inspections and professional roles.
steps: Choose buying, selling or reviewing a transaction.
List key dates and contingencies privately.
Identify title, inspection, financing and disclosure questions.
Confirm each professional's role and duty.
Seek qualified Tennessee review before signing or waiving rights.
questions: Which deadlines or contingencies matter?
Who verifies title and disclosures?
What should receive qualified review before signing?

tracks.title: Rental, repair or deposit preparation
tracks.summary: Organize lease, condition, communication and date facts without deciding legal rights.
steps: Choose repair, access, deposit, notice or lease concern.
Record dates and communications privately.
Keep copies of the lease, notices and condition evidence under your control.
Identify the responsible property contact and official starting route.
Seek qualified Tennessee help for legal conclusions or urgent deadlines.
questions: What does the written lease say?
Which facts and notices should be preserved?
Which Tennessee resource can confirm next steps?

tracks.title: Contractor and project readiness
tracks.summary: Compare project scope, credentials, estimates, changes and completion terms consistently.
steps: Write one consistent project scope for every estimate.
Verify licensing when applicable and insurance directly.
Compare price, allowances, exclusions, schedule and change-order terms.
Identify permit and inspection responsibilities.
Keep approval, payment and warranty records privately.
questions: What is included and excluded?
Who handles permits and inspections?
How are changes, payments and warranties documented?

auto.label: Auto and vehicle preparation
auto.boundary: General vehicle preparation only—not mechanical diagnosis, legal advice, repair authorization, insurance determination, dealer endorsement or a safety guarantee. Stop driving and use emergency help when a vehicle may be unsafe.
auto.todayBoundary: For a crash with injuries or immediate danger, call 911. If the vehicle may be unsafe to drive, stop in a safe place and contact qualified roadside or repair help.

tracks.title: Repair estimate and authorization
tracks.summary: Separate diagnosis, estimate, authorization and completion review.
steps: Describe symptoms without diagnosing the cause.
Ask for inspection and estimate terms.
Confirm what requires additional authorization.
Record parts, labor, warranty and completion questions.
Review the final invoice against authorized work.
questions: What testing supports the recommendation?
What requires approval before work continues?
What warranty applies?

tracks.title: Recall and safety readiness
tracks.summary: Prepare VIN-based recall verification and safe next steps at the responsible source.
steps: Stop driving when the vehicle may be unsafe.
Use the official NHTSA VIN recall lookup privately.
Confirm remedy status with an authorized service provider.
Ask about transportation and timing before travel.
Keep completion documentation under your control.
questions: Is there an open recall for this VIN?
Is the vehicle safe to drive until repair?
How is remedy completion documented?

tracks.title: Title and registration preparation
tracks.summary: Prepare ownership, lien and Tennessee documentation questions before visiting the responsible office.
steps: Choose title, registration, plate, lien or transfer need.
Confirm the responsible Tennessee or county office.
Use the official checklist for your transaction type.
Prepare originals and copies without uploading them here.
Verify fees, payment methods and appointment rules directly.
checklist: Fees and visit details to verify
questions: Which office handles this transaction?
Which originals are required?
Which fees and visit rules are current?

tracks.title: Vehicle purchase or dispute preparation
tracks.summary: Organize advertised, written, inspection, warranty and communication facts before qualified review.
steps: Separate advertisement, written agreement and spoken statements.
Arrange an independent inspection when appropriate.
Confirm title, lien, recall and warranty facts.
Keep communications and records privately.
Prepare neutral questions for the seller, agency or qualified professional.
questions: Which promises are written?
What did an independent inspection find?
Which remedy or review route should I verify?
